key_insight: Encoder–decoder operator learning can be analyzed in a resolution-independent way by passing to a limiting kernel, so approximation guarantees no longer depend on the particular input/output discretization.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a principled path to design and compare operator-learning models, encoder choices, and neural architectures across different resolutions while retaining predictable error and complexity behavior.
method: Map finite-dimensional encoded data to a matrix-valued kernel that induces an operator-valued kernel on the original function spaces.
Prove convergence of these induced kernels to a limiting kernel via operator-norm convergence of the associated integral operators.
Derive upper and lower error bounds for regularized SGD and extend the theory to encoder–decoder neural networks through the limiting NTK.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical upper and lower bounds, including optimization terms of order t^{-θ} and T^{-θ′}, plus an additional finite-width term and polynomial complexity guarantees when encoding errors decay algebraically.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on asymptotic kernel convergence and encoding-error decay, so finite-resolution discretizations or mismatched encoders may weaken the stated bounds in practice.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
